solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Residue of distillation in bowl

definitions.meaning: the black tarry substance left after distilling tar or turpentine
in cricket, to deliver the ball so that it bounces before the batter

explanation.surface: Something left over from distilling sits in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions; 'bowl' looks like a noun for a dish but is the cricket verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to one word: the tarry distillation residue, and the cricket verb for delivering the ball.

clue.text: Standard recess containing head of Hermes artist put differently

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: containing says the recess holds the next pieces

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess in a church

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word Hermes

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A standard alcove holding a bust of Hermes by an artist, phrased another way.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, so it is crossword shorthand for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Restating text in other words is a rewording of it.

clue.text: Obtain money from dancing

definitions.meaning: to ask someone for a loan or gift, as in touch a friend for cash
a style of dance using shoes with metal plates that click on the floor

explanation.surface: Earning a living by dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both: wheedling cash out of someone, and the clicking dance style.

clue.text: Bird having ring round middle of leg

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
O is round in shape

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word leg

explanation.surface: A bird with a ring round the middle of its leg, as ringers do.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinkish crested bird of Europe, Asia and Africa.

clue.text: Turns around, caught by rotter in hopeless endeavour

indicators.note: caught by says one piece is held inside the word for rotter

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person, a rotter

indicators.note: around tells us the word for turns is read back to front

parts.note: acts, as in variety turns or performances

explanation.surface: Someone spinning round and getting grabbed by a scoundrel in a doomed effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' tempts as the cricket C, but 'caught by' is the container signal; 'Turns' are stage acts, turned 'around' to give STCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an undertaking with no chance of success is called a hopeless cause.

clue.text: Trailer inhabited by poor Sioux having no vote in state

indicators.note: inhabited by says the plant has the jumbled letters living inside it

parts.note: a liana is a trailing, climbing plant of tropical forests

indicators.note: poor says the remaining letters are in a bad, jumbled state
having no says the vote mark is dropped from the word

parts.note: the Sioux are a Native American people
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A trailer park home to impoverished Sioux without the vote in some US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a caravan, but it is a trailing plant. SIOUX 'having no' X leaves SIOU, which 'poor' reshuffles to OUIS.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty states of the USA, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Measures employed by chaste psychic

indicators.note: employed by says the letters are found at work inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Methods used by a pure-minded clairvoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: Actions taken to achieve something, as in take measures or take action.

clue.text: Hold racket with hand and run

parts.note: a racket is a con, a swindle
a side, as in on the one hand
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Grip a tennis racket in one hand and run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' means regard as, believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hold an opinion is to regard or deem something to be so.

clue.text: Not becoming joined, divided by new taunt

indicators.note: divided by says the word for joined is split by the other pieces

parts.note: unified means joined together
a dig is a jibe or taunt

explanation.surface: Not looking good when united and then split by a fresh insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is the adjective meaning seemly, not the verb. The jibe goes in before the N, against the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means seemly or befitting; lacking dignity is unseemly.

clue.text: Secure approach, first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: to near is to approach

explanation.surface: Lock in your approach from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR has its first letter, N, moved 'first to last'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to secure a reward or win something by effort is to gain it.

clue.text: Copy expert breaking contract

indicators.note: breaking says the word for expert splits the word for contract open

parts.note: to contract is to shrink or reduce
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist breaking an agreement, with a copy of the document involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' reads as a noun, an agreement, but is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to duplicate or imitate something is to make a replica of it.

clue.text: Clear article about most unsuccessful point

indicators.note: about tells us the two pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to rid is to clear, as in rid the house of mice
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A plain piece of writing about the low point of a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole of RID + AN, giving the letters back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, a rock-bottom moment, is its nadir in figurative use.

clue.text: Important to keep group of law enforcers winning

indicators.note: to keep says the word for important holds the group inside it

parts.note: pressing means urgent, important
a posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law

explanation.surface: It matters to retain a police unit that is coming out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' is the adjective meaning charming, not victorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a winning manner is attractive and makes a favourable first impression.

clue.text: Foolish editor accepting distortion of a deep myth

indicators.note: accepting says the editor takes the anagram inside
distortion of says the letters of a deep myth are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A silly editor swallowing a twisted version of a profound legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the three words gives MPTYHEADE, the nine letters that sit between the editor's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking sense or intelligence, with nothing in the brain.

clue.text: Criminal out in company with naughty, wealthy elite

indicators.note: in says the anagram goes inside the company letters

parts.note: plc is a public limited company

indicators.note: criminal says the letters of out are bent into another order

parts.note: racy means risqué, naughty

explanation.surface: A crook out on the town with a rich, naughty set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges OUT to UTO, placed 'in' PLC.
explanation.definitionFit: Government or dominance by the rich, a ruling class of the wealthy.

clue.text: King with suitable intent

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
apt means suitable, fitting

explanation.surface: A monarch with a fitting purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' reads as a noun, purpose, but is the adjective meaning absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone wholly absorbed or engrossed in something is intent upon it.

clue.text: Fellow referring to air about good executive

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: about says the phrase for referring to air goes round the letter for good

parts.note: aerial means relating to the air

explanation.surface: A chap talking about the atmosphere around a decent boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executive' looks like a noun, a boss, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: executive functions are those of running or directing an organisation, the work of those in charge.

clue.text: Owl may see unusually impressively

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of owl may see are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: An owl might see in an remarkably impressive manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a way that inspires wonder or great admiration.

clue.text: In charge, upset staff holding on for dessert

indicators.note: holding says the turned staff keeps the word for on inside
upset in a down clue says the word for staff is turned upside down

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: The person in charge, upset that staff are holding on to the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: MACE 'upset' gives ECAM, which holds RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen sweet made of cream or custard, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Resistance on island occupied by fight for tower

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the resistance letter after the rest
occupied by says the island has the fight inside it

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
a scrap is a fight
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters on an island taken over by a battle for a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island off western Scotland. 'Resistance' tempts as a wartime movement, but it is just the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building is a tower block; a skyscraper is the extreme example.

clue.text: Handle greeting by officer

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Lt is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Coping with a salute from an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The grip of a sword or dagger is its handle.

clue.text: Make fun of old-fashioned stew

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
out means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Mock an outdated casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly seasoned French dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly.

clue.text: Comprehensive delicacy once in arrangement involving piano

indicators.note: involving says the anagram takes in the letter for piano
in arrangement says the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A thorough treat from long ago, part of a musical piece with piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives ENCYCLOAEDIC, and 'involving' slips the piano letter in after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: covering all subjects or a vast range of knowledge, as a reference work does.

clue.text: Island's top centre for tourists

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: centre for picks the two middle letters of the word tourists

explanation.surface: An island is the top destination for holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian isle in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Try one move on ground before take-off

parts.note: to tax is to strain or try, as in tax one's patience
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Attempt a single shift of position before departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Of an aircraft, to travel slowly along the runway under its own power.

clue.text: Get rotten burden, not small

indicators.note: not says the letter for small is left out

parts.note: to saddle someone is to burden them

explanation.surface: Something going off becomes a load, though not a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' is a verb here: SADDLE loses S.
explanation.definitionFit: Of an egg, to go bad or putrid; the verb survives in addled eggs.

clue.text: Flower power, on reflection, stopped by hard facts

indicators.note: stopped by says the hard letter plugs the gap inside

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

indicators.note: on reflection says the flower is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: an anemone is a flower
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Flower power, looked back on, brought up short by hard facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower power' reads as the 1960s slogan but splits into two pieces; the reflected flower gives ENOMENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Observable events or occurrences, things that are known to happen or exist.

clue.text: Complete crook ignoring bishop

indicators.note: ignoring says the bishop letter is left out

parts.note: a crook is a bend, as in the crook of the arm
B is bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: An utter crook pays no attention to the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' is a curve, not a criminal; 'Complete' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to complete something is to finish or conclude it.

clue.text: Protection from popular god sheltering maiden and knight

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: sheltering says the god holds the two letters inside

parts.note: a deity is a god
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: Shelter from a popular god who shields a young woman and a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Security against loss or damage, as given by an insurance guarantee of compensation.

clue.text: Drink's temperature not even variable

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: A drink's temperature is unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot mixed drink of spirits, sugar and water.
